question: In March 2025, India introduced anti-dumping duties on five products imported from which country?
solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anti-dumping duties are imposed to protect domestic industries from unfair trade practices such as the dumping of cheap foreign goods at below-market prices.
 
• India introduced anti-dumping duties on five products originating from China in March 2025, aiming to prevent harm to local manufacturers.
 
• The targeted products included chemicals, steel products, and consumer goods, which were found to be sold below fair market value.
 
• This action was taken following investigations by the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• The duties are compliant with WTO norms, ensuring fair trade while safeguarding India's economic interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-Dumping Duty:**

 
 
• It is a protectionist tariff imposed by a government on imports that are priced below their normal value in the exporting country.
 
• Aims to safeguard domestic industries from predatory pricing practices by foreign exporters.
 
• Dumping can lead to market distortions and long-term damage to domestic production capabilities.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO) Guidelines:**
 
 
• Anti-dumping measures must comply with WTO’s Anti-Dumping Agreement.
 
• Governments must conduct investigations to prove dumping and its impact on domestic industries.
 
• WTO allows countries to impose duties only to the extent necessary to counteract harm caused by dumping.
 
 
 
• **Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR):**
 
 
• It is India's apex authority for investigating unfair trade practices such as dumping and subsidies.
 
• DGTR operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• It recommends anti-dumping duties and countervailing measures based on its investigations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Anti-Dumping Duties:**
 
 
• Protects domestic industries from unfair competition.
 
• Encourages fair pricing and trade practices globally.
 
• May lead to increased prices for consumers but is aimed at ensuring long-term economic stability.
